caseno: Appeal from Original Order No 379 of 1980
lawyer:
S.R. Pal with S.K.M. Saifuddin Ahmed and S.K. Sinha ----- For the Appellant
S.C. Das ----- For Respondent No.1
M. Hafizullah with Mahbubey Alam ----- For Respondent No.2.
parties:
M/S Monty Tannery Ltd ----- Appellant
Vs.
Zulaikha & another ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Abdul Matin Khan Chowdhury, J.-This appeal is at the instance of auction-purchaser filed against the order dated 21st April, 1980 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong in Miscellaneous Case No. 203 of 1979 under Order 21, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The appeal arises out of 'an application filed under Order 21, rule 90 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the auction sale held on 13.7.76 in Mortgage Execution Case No.2 of 1976. 

 2. Facts in short are that the Decree Holder Bank got a decree in mortgage suit No. 35 of 1966 against M/s. Gulistan Tanneries of which the petitioner's father was a partner. The decree-holder having filed mortgage execution case No. 2/76 for satisfaction of the decretal amount on sale of 3.77 acres of land and structures thereon On the basis of the said petition a sale proclamation was issued but the structures on the land described in the petition was not included in the proclamation. It is the case of the Judgment debtor that the sale proclamation was not published according to law and no notice was given in the Court premises or to the Collectorate and there was material irregularities and fraud in publishing and conducting the sale. It was further alleged by the Judgment-debtor that the sale was seriously under-valued and properties worth more than Tk. 10,00,000/- were sold for Taka 1,65,000/- only. Thus the Judgment-debtor was seriously prejudiced due to material irregularities and fraud hence the sale was liable to be set aside. The decree-holder contested the said petition by filing a written objection denying the allegations made in the petition. The decree-holder stated in their objection that the Judgment debtor petitioner has got no right or locus standi to file and to maintain the present petition under Order 21, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It was asserted by the decree holder that the sale proclamation was duly prepared and legally published and the property in question were not undervalued in the sale proclamation. The property in question was sold for proper and' adequate value and this petition for setting aside the sale was a device to delay the execution of the decree. Hence the said application was liable to be dismissed. The learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of the materials on record allowed the application and set aside the auction sale held on 13.7.76. Being aggrieved the decree- holder has preferred this First Miscellaneous Appeal before this Court. 

 4. Mr. S.C. Das, the learned Counsel has appeared on behalf of the Respondent No.1. He submits that the Respondent No.1 Mrs. Zulekha, daughter of the Judgment debtor was competent to file the application under Order 21, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the sale. He further submits that she filed this application on behalf of the Judgment debtor by virtue of a Power filed by the Judgment debtor. Mr. S.C. Das has referred to a decision of the Appellate Division reported in 29 D.L.R. (S.C.) page 185. It appears that Money Suit No. 35 of 1966 was decreed. The decree- holder started execution case in the year 1976. It is an admitted fact that Mr. Ebrahim Karim was one of the Partners of the firm viz. Gulistan Tannery. He left Bangladesh in May, 1971 and came back to Bangladesh on 2nd September, 1976. The sale in question took place on 13.7.1976 by virtue of Mortgage Execution Case No. 2 of 1976. Mrs. Zulekha, the daughter of Mr. Ibrahim Karim was all along in Bangladesh. She filed this application under Order 21, rule 90 read withsection 151 C.P.C. for setting aside the auction sale held on 13.7.76. It further appears that Mrs. Zulekha filed the petition for herself and as well as on behalf of her father Mr. Ibrahim Karim. The application was filed by Mrs. Zulekha under Order 21, rule 90 read with section 151 C.P.C. The Cause Title of the said application was in the following terms:- 

 5. From the above it is clear that Mrs. Zulekha filed the said application on behalf of herself as well as on behalf of Mr. Ebrahim Karim, the Managing Partner of Gulistan Tannery the Judgment-debtor. It appears that Mr. Ebrahim Karim was examined in his case. He stated in his deposition "I have filed this petition through my daughter Mrs. Zulekha. I duly gave her Power of Attorney. I am the proprietor of Messrs Gulistan Tannery formerly it was a Partnership firm with brother and father. The disputed property mortgaged to Chartered Bank O.P. No.1. The D. Hr.O.P.1 filed Mortgage Suit No. 35/62. The disputed property compromises 3.44 acres of land, residential pucca building, factory building with two sets tannery machineries one of which were of English origin. The value of the landed properties alone is Rs. 10,00,000/-. I appeared in the mortgage suit. In May, 1971 I left Bangladesh. The first decree was passed on 19.6.75 when I was not here, I was not aware of Mort, Execution Case No.2 of 1976 filed on 9.1.1976. No notice was served upon me. No notice of sale was also served on 4.6.76". 

 7. From the above, it is clear that an interest of a person in the property sold can file an application under Order 21, rule 90 C.P.C. for setting aside of the sale. In the present case although the petition was filed by Mrs. Zulekha, but it was actually filed on behalf of her father who was a Judgment debtor. In this view of the matter the application filed under Order 21, rule 90. C.P.C. by Zulekha is quite maintainable as she was duly authorised to file the said application. Mr. Pal next submits that the learned Subordinate Judge was not correct in holding that the notice of the sale was not properly served on the Judgment debtor. It appears that the learned Subordinate Judge while considering the question on service of the notice has considered the evidence of O.P.W.2 who stated that there were tea-stalls and three pan-biri shops within 200 cubits of the suit tannery, but no witnesses was produced from that area besides no person was named in the notice as witness. He also referred to the deposition of O.P. No.1 that many people gathered together at the time of beating of drum. But no independent person was found to attest the notice of service of the said proclamation. It appears from the deposition of O.P. No.1 who said in his cross-examination "I did not know the disputed tannery from before. I went to the D.Hr. Bank on the day of service. I do not remember how many people accompanied me. I went to the Bank from the Court. I do not remember at what time I reached the disputed site. The drummer was taken by man of decree-holder. The beating of drum was started on reaching the disputed tannery. Some people gathered there. I found a man in the verandah of the suit tannery. I got him as a witness. The two witnesses belonged to Monti Tannery. Not a fact there was no other persons except the witnesses and man of D. Hr. at the time of alleged service".
